Oct 26, 2026

Advanced Nameservers use a nameserver type

DNS

Starting today, the DNS settings endpoints gradually begin to represent Advanced Nameservers with nameservers.type: "cloudflare.advanced". The rollout is expected to take seven days. Previously, the API used the "foundation_dns": true setting for this configuration.

Before the rollout reaches an account, the endpoints continue to return nameservers.type: "cloudflare.standard" for Advanced Nameservers. The endpoints accept nameservers.type: "cloudflare.advanced" in PATCH requests for entitled accounts throughout the rollout. The zone settings JSON for /zones/{zone_id}/dns_settings is:

Cloudflare will make an equivalent change to /accounts/{account_id}/dns_settings at the same time.

The foundation_dns boolean remains available as a deprecated compatibility alias in zone and account-default settings. Use nameservers.type: "cloudflare.advanced" for new writes.

You can continue to read and write foundation_dns during this transition. If a PATCH request includes both values, they must match. The API rejects conflicting values.

Update clients that treat nameservers.type as a closed enum to recognize the "cloudflare.advanced" value.

This API update does not change your Foundation DNS subscription or whether Advanced Nameservers are enabled on your zones. It does not require a zone migration.

In a future API change, Cloudflare will remove the foundation_dns parameter from the API endpoint. After migrating to nameservers.type, remove handling for the boolean from your client.

Oct 26, 2026

Workers tracing — new spanContext(), setStatus(), and updateName() APIs

Workers

Custom spans in Workers now support three more methods from the OpenTelemetry span API.

  • span.spanContext() returns the span's traceId, spanId, and traceFlags. The IDs match the trace and span IDs in Workers Observability and in exported traces, so you can log them or return them to clients to correlate a request with its trace.
  • span.setStatus(status) sets the span status to "unset", "ok", or "error", with an optional message for errors. Span status is included in traces exported to OpenTelemetry destinations. The Workers Observability dashboard does not display it yet.
  • span.updateName(name) renames a span after it starts, such as once you know which route a request matched. You can also rename the invocation's root span returned by tracing.getActiveSpan().

For more details, refer to the custom spans documentation.

Oct 25, 2026

WAF Release - 2026-10-25 - Emergency - Cloudflare Managed Ruleset

WAF

This emergency release will add two rules related to the Brotli vulnerability CVE-2026-111497 ↗︎ to the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset. Both rules will be enabled by default with their action set to Log, providing visibility into matching requests so customers can evaluate the impact before choosing to block them.

Rule behavior

  • Brotli rule: Matches incoming requests that declare Brotli request-body encoding (Content-Encoding: br), including legitimate clients submitting Brotli-encoded request bodies. It does not match Accept-Encoding: br or affect Cloudflare's Brotli response-compression settings. The rule's default action is Log.
  • Next.js rule: Matches requests to the Next.js image optimization endpoint (/_next/image), including legitimate image optimization traffic. The default action is Log and does not block requests. Changing the action to Block may prevent optimized images from loading and disrupt image delivery for applications using this endpoint.

Default behavior

  • Both rules will log matching requests without blocking them when the ruleset defaults are used.
  • Customers will be able to review matches in analytics and configure a blocking action for either rule if desired.
  • Enabling these rules in Log mode provides visibility only; it does not block requests matching these rules.

Important: Check existing action overrides

If you have configured a ruleset-level action override that applies Block to these rules, matching requests may be blocked as soon as the rules are deployed, despite their default Log action. This may result in false positives and block legitimate traffic.

Review your existing ruleset overrides before deployment. If you want to evaluate these rules without blocking traffic, configure rule-specific overrides to use Log and review matching requests before switching to Block.

Oct 23, 2026

D1 database undelete requests limited to the last 7 days

D1

The D1 undelete API now only accepts requests for databases that were deleted within the last 7 days. Requests to undelete a database that was deleted more than 7 days ago will fail and return an error.

If you delete a D1 database by mistake, send the undelete request as soon as possible, and no later than 7 days after deletion.

For more information, refer to the undelete D1 database API reference.

Oct 23, 2026

Target Flagship feature flags with structured evaluation context

Flagship

Flagship supports nested objects, arrays, and null in evaluation context. Pass user profiles and tag lists directly, then target nested attributes without flattening your application data.

For example, pass a profile and tags when evaluating a flag through the Workers binding:

A targeting rule can combine profile.plan equals "enterprise" with tags has "beta" to serve the feature to enterprise users in the beta group. Use dot-separated paths for nested attributes and the has and not_has operators for array membership. Percentage rollouts can also use a nested identifier, such as profile.id, for consistent user assignment.

Structured context works through the Workers binding, the evaluation REST API with a JSON POST body, and the TypeScript, Python, and Go OpenFeature SDKs from version 0.6.0. The SDKs automatically use POST when HTTP evaluation requires structured context.

Refer to targeting rules, the evaluation API, and SDK context support for usage and supported values.

Redesigned Cloudflare Radar homepage

Radar

The Cloudflare Radar homepage has been redesigned to make global Internet data easier to explore for broader audiences, including journalists, policymakers, and everyday users, while preserving the depth that technical users rely on.

  • Interactive map: Shows Internet traffic and outages around the world, and acts as a starting point for exploring specific countries and trends.
  • Curated insights section: Tabbed navigation that highlights summary statistics across Radar data, with a call to action to explore each area in depth.
  • Updated interface: Built with Kumo ↗︎ components, the same ones used across Cloudflare products.

As we continue the redesign, all Radar pages will see improvements. Share feedback at radar@cloudflare.com.

For more details, read the blog post ↗︎ or visit Cloudflare Radar ↗︎.

Oct 23, 2026

Workers Builds and Pages build images reject compromised eMudhra certificates

WorkersPages

The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities ↗︎ can be recovered, so anyone can forge a certificate for any hostname that chains to them. The Workers Builds and Pages build images now reject these certificates when your build clones your repository, installs dependencies, or makes HTTPS requests.

The updated images include patched CA certificates, Node.js 22.23.4 and 24.22.1, Bun 1.4.4, and pip 26.2.2. Build commands also run with environment variables that point older runtimes at the patched CA certificates.

What you need to do

Most projects need no changes. Update your project if:

  • You set BUN_VERSION below 1.4.4. Older Bun versions trust the compromised certificates.
  • You set your own SSL_CERT_FILE, PIP_CERT, or REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, or set --use-bundled-ca in NODE_OPTIONS. Make sure your CA certificates do not trust the compromised intermediates.
  • Your build installs tools that ship their own CA certificates. Update them to a version that removes the compromised intermediates.

For details, refer to the build image documentation for Workers Builds and Pages.

Oct 23, 2026

Pin your npm version in Workers Builds with packageManager

Workers

You can now choose the npm version that Workers Builds uses by setting the packageManager field in your package.json. Before the build installs dependencies, it installs the npm version you set, so a lockfile written by a newer npm version installs the same way in your build as it does locally.

The packageManager field also sets the version of Yarn, pnpm, and Bun. Use an exact version, such as npm@11.19.1, not a range. Workers Builds does not use the engines.npm field to choose an npm version.

For more information, refer to Package manager versions.

Oct 22, 2026

Cloudflare One Client for Windows (version 2026.9.1555.1)

Cloudflare One Client

A new Beta release for the Windows Cloudflare One Client is now available on the beta releases downloads page.

This release includes the following highlights:

  • Added automatic endpoint selection for Global Acceleration. When Global Acceleration is enabled for an organization, the client connects to the Global Acceleration endpoints while the device is in the acceleration region and to the standard anycast endpoints otherwise, and reconnects when a network change moves the device between them without requiring action from the user. The Connectivity page shows which tunnel and API endpoints are in use, and users who are allowed to override the selection can choose endpoints in Settings.
  • Added protection against unauthorized modification or uninstallation of the Cloudflare One Client. When enabled, the user will be asked to provide an administrator-generated code when trying to uninstall the client, which will otherwise be blocked.
  • The client now shows a banner when the network limits the tunnel MTU to a degraded or critically low value. The banner clears when the MTU recovers or the client disconnects.

Additional Changes and improvements

  • The client now applies tunnel MTUs between 1147 and 1199 bytes measured by Path MTU Discovery. Previously the client ignored these values and kept a larger MTU, which could drop larger packets on networks such as mobile hotspots while the client showed as connected.
  • When Path MTU Discovery is enabled, the client now accepts larger packets from Cloudflare instead of limiting them to the size it uses for its own outbound packets.
  • Access reauthentication requests now trust certificates in the operating system's certificate store, so reauthentication works on networks that perform TLS inspection.
  • For Zero Trust deployments, the client now records a traceroute of the network path outside the tunnel when the tunnel degrades or fails to connect. warp-diag includes the same trace.
  • warp-diag now includes redacted copies of the deployed MDM files and the names, but not the values, of stored registration secrets. It reports a QUIC path MTU only when one was measured.
  • Added the MDM parameters mdm_file_debounce_secs (1–60) and mdm_file_unavailable_debounce_secs (0–300), which set how long the client waits before applying a changed MDM file and before acting on a missing or unreadable one.
  • The consumer client home screen now shows when the connection is post-quantum encrypted.
  • The client UI no longer starts WMIC or PowerShell processes to collect memory information for crash reports.
  • Fixed a hostname-based split tunnel entry not taking effect until the next reconnect after its firewall rule failed to apply.
  • Fixed the client window appearing blank or white after an upgrade, at sign-in, after waking from sleep, or after a display change.
  • Fixed the client service restarting when a firewall update for captive portal detection stalled while the device was asleep.
  • Fixed the client getting stuck in a disconnected state on Windows on Arm devices because leftover tunnel adapters were not removed.
  • Fixed the client being unable to connect after an upgrade, downgrade, and upgrade that switched between consumer and Zero Trust registrations. The client now clears the mismatched registration so the user can register again.
  • Fixed the client UI looking for one of its libraries in a directory that standard users can create before looking in the installation directory.
  • Fixed warp-cli registration license reporting an error on slow networks even though the license was applied, which left the client registered to a WARP+ account it did not recognize.
  • Fixed Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX) results being reported with timestamps offset from the actual time after the system clock was corrected.
  • Added the MDM parameters managed_network_probe_interval_secs (30–300, default 30) and managed_network_probe_count (0 disables probing, 1–10, or -1 to keep probing until a managed network is found; default 1). After a registration or network change finds no managed network, the client now rechecks, so a device doesn't stay on the default profile because of a transient connection failure. Set the count to 0 to keep the previous behavior.
  • In proxy mode for Zero Trust, the client now sends hostnames from HTTP/HTTPS and SOCKS5 requests to Cloudflare for resolution instead of resolving them on the device.
  • When the app cannot reach the client service, the home screen now says why (service not running, not accepting connections, not responding, or connection dropped and reconnecting). It shows an error code and a Learn more link instead of "IPC error".
  • Fixed Windows resetting the Wi-Fi adapter after sign-in or a Wi-Fi restart when the client's firewall rules in Exclude split tunnel mode blocked Windows network connectivity checks. The client now allows those checks.
  • Fixed the installer asking the user to close running applications during an upgrade, downgrade or uninstall because other programs loaded the client's Visual C++ runtime libraries through the system PATH. The client now loads these libraries from a private folder so that closing other applications is unnecessary.

Known issues

A Windows DNS client regression may cause connectivity check failures on systems containing large hosts files. While our client includes a mitigation for this issue, users may still experience reduced DNS performance and connectivity check failures.

For Zero Trust documentation please see: https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/ For Consumer documentation please see: https://developers.cloudflare.com/warp-client/

The client now keeps the last applied policy for 20 seconds after the file becomes unavailable.   • Fixed Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX) results being reported with timestamps offset from the actual time after the system clock was corrected.
  • Fixed an upgrade sometimes leaving the client without a running service when the previous service was slow to stop. The installer now waits up to 10 seconds for the old service to be removed before starting the new one.
  • Fixed the OS version detail stored for a device keeping an outdated value, including the text "Usage: sw_vers…" reported by client versions 2023.5.587.1 through 2024.12.760.0. The client now clears the value the next time it connects.
  • Added the MDM parameters managed_network_probe_interval_secs (30–300, default 30) and managed_network_probe_count (0 disables probing, 1–10, or -1 to keep probing until a managed network is found; default 1). After a registration or network change finds no managed network, the client now rechecks, so a device doesn't stay on the default profile because of a transient connection failure. Set the count to 0 to keep the previous behavior.
  • In proxy mode for Zero Trust, the client now sends hostnames from HTTP/HTTPS and SOCKS5 requests to Cloudflare for resolution, instead of resolving them on the device.
  • When the app cannot reach the client service, the home screen now says why (service not running, not accepting connections, not responding, or connection dropped and reconnecting). It shows an error code and a Learn more link instead of "IPC error".

None.

Cloudflare MCP servers no longer serve /sse

Agents

Cloudflare's product-specific MCP servers now serve only /mcp. A request to /sse returns 410 Gone with the server's /mcp URL, which most MCP clients show in their connection error.

If your MCP client is configured with an /sse URL, change it to /mcp, for example https://docs.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp. If you signed in through /sse, your client asks you to sign in again. Connections that already use /mcp are not affected.

Oct 22, 2026

Agents SDK now supports the latest Pi 1.4 release

Agents

Agents SDK v0.30.0 runs PiHarness on Pi 1.4 ↗︎, and makes it recover more reliably from evictions, crashes, and storage errors.

  • Hibernation while Pi's tasks sleep. PiHarness passes Pi's new onWake callback to your harness factory. While a task sleeps, such as during a model retry backoff, the Durable Object can hibernate until the task is due instead of staying in memory.
  • Parked tasks. Pi 1.4 parks a task that keeps crashing the object instead of restarting it forever. Parked operations show as parked in pending(), and session.retry() runs them again.
  • Recovery from storage errors. PiHarness reopens Pi after a storage error instead of failing every call until the object restarts. Its wake-up job retries failed steps with a backoff instead of being dropped.
  • Retried model streams. agents/models/pi-ai reports a cut-off or idle model stream as a transient error, so Pi retries the turn instead of failing it.

Upgrade

The Agents SDK v0.30.0 changelog ↗︎ has step-by-step upgrade instructions. Point your coding agent at them and upgrade today:

Pi 1.4 migrates the session storage in the object's SQLite database to a schema that Pi 1.3 cannot open, so a deployment cannot roll back past this upgrade. Refer to the Pi Durable 1.4.0 changelog ↗︎ for Pi's own breaking changes.

Oct 22, 2026

Sandbox SDK 0.12.14 updates trusted certificates after the eMudhra compromise

Sandboxes

The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities ↗︎ can be recovered, so anyone can forge a certificate for any hostname that chains to them. Sandbox SDK images before 0.12.14 trust these certificates. An HTTPS connection that leaves the container directly, such as one from mountBucket(), backups, gitCheckout(), tunnels, or code that runs in the sandbox, can be intercepted with a forged certificate.

What you need to do

Sandbox SDK 0.x

Update immediately. Install @cloudflare/sandbox@0.12.14, change the FROM line in your Dockerfile to the matching image, and redeploy. Keep any -python, -opencode, or -musl suffix on the image tag. The deployment's rollout replaces running sandboxes with ones that use the new image.

If you use the next prerelease, update to 0.13.0-next.825.1 or later.

If you cannot update yet and use 0.8.7 or later, send all HTTPS through your Worker, so that Cloudflare checks every certificate on port 443 whatever your image trusts:

Deploy, then stop running sandboxes so that they restart with the interception certificate. This does not cover TLS on other ports, such as cloudflared tunnels, and clients that ignore the injected certificate fail to connect. For more information, refer to HTTPS traffic.

Sandbox SDK 1.x

You do not need to update the SDK, because it makes no TLS connections of its own. Your image decides which certificates your sandboxes trust, so rebuild it and replace the sandboxes that run the old one:

  1. Run docker pull for each base image in your Dockerfile, then clear the Docker build cache with docker builder prune --all. wrangler deploy builds with your local images and build cache, so without these steps it can ship the old CA certificates and runtimes. If your Wrangler configuration references an image by digest, build and push a new image and update the digest instead.
  2. Deploy your Worker.
  3. Stop sandboxes that are still running, for example with this.ctx.container.destroy(). A running sandbox keeps the image it started with until it stops. To restart only the sandboxes whose image is out of date, refer to Roll out a named image update.
  4. If you use snapshots, create new ones from sandboxes that run the updated image. A snapshot restores the image it was created from, so an older snapshot brings back the old certificates.

Check your sandboxes

From inside a sandbox, connect to one of the test hosts listed at emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com ↗︎ with each TLS client your code uses, such as curl, node, or bun. Every request should fail:

What changed in 0.12.13 and 0.12.14

In the 0.12.13 images, the system CA bundle, Node.js, cloudflared, and pip reject certificates from the compromised intermediates. The images ship updated Ubuntu and Alpine CA certificates, Node.js 22.23.4, cloudflared 2026.10.2, and pip 26.2.2 in the -python image.

0.12.14 updates Bun to 1.4.4, so the bun command and createBackup() uploads of archives of 10 MiB or more reject these certificates too. The -opencode image ships OpenCode 1.19.4 or later, which also runs on Bun 1.4.4.

Cloudflare Tunnel supports URL normalization

Cloudflare TunnelCloudflare Tunnel for SASE

Starting from version 2026.10.0, Cloudflare Tunnel can normalize URLs before matching ingress rules. This improves security for tunnels with rules that require Cloudflare Access validation. The URL path sent to your origin stays the same.

In three months, starting 2027-01-25, new cloudflared releases will turn on URL normalization by default. Test your path-based routing before that date, as this change may affect which ingress rule matches a request. Configurations without rules requiring Access validation are unaffected.

This setting is currently off by default. To turn it on, run:

Alternatively, set TUNNEL_DISABLE_PATH_NORMALIZATION=false on each cloudflared replica and restart it.

For more information, refer to ingress matching and Access validation at the origin.

Granular Tunnel Read And Monitor role is generally available

Cloudflare FundamentalsCloudflare OneCloudflare Tunnel for SASECloudflare Tunnel

The Cloudflare Tunnel - Granular Connector cloudflared Read And Monitor role is now generally available. You can grant a member read access and log streaming for specific Cloudflare Tunnel instances without granting write access or access to every Tunnel in your account.

This role includes the same access as Cloudflare Tunnel - Granular Connector cloudflared Read: viewing selected Tunnels, their IP and hostname routes, and connector host details. It also grants remote log streaming, so support operators can troubleshoot a Tunnel without changing its configuration. The existing Read role does not grant log streaming access.

To assign the role, follow Grant a granular permission. For the available roles, refer to the resource-scoped roles reference.

Oct 21, 2026

createAI replaces workers-ai-provider and ai-gateway-provider

AgentsWorkers AIAI Gateway

The Agents SDK has a new createAI function for the AI SDK and Pi AI. It unifies what workers-ai-provider and ai-gateway-provider did: Workers AI models, AI Gateway catalog models, dynamic routes, and vendor models, through the AI binding or an account id and API token.

workers-ai-provider and ai-gateway-provider are now feature frozen and marked as deprecated. Please migrate at your convenience.

With createAI you get:

  • Every model by id. Workers AI @cf/ ids, any model in the AI Gateway catalog, and dynamic routes as dynamic/<route>.
  • Vendor model objects. Pass a model from the vendor's own package, such as ai(anthropic("claude-opus-5-5")). It goes unchanged to AI Gateway's provider-native endpoint.
  • The binding, or an account id and API token. Use a gateway in another account, or call from outside a Worker.
  • Gateway options, fallback, and BYOK. Caching, logging, metadata, retries, byokAlias, zdr, and vendorKey.
  • Stream resume. Through the binding, a catalog or dynamic route stream that drops mid-answer resumes.
  • Other model types. Embeddings, images, speech, transcription, and reranking in the AI SDK provider, and images in Pi AI.
Before After
createWorkersAI({ binding }) createAI({ binding })
createWorkersAI({ accountId, apiKey }) createAI({ accountId, apiToken })
createAiGateway(...) createAI(...), with fallback for a list of models
createAISearch from workers-ai-provider createAISearchNamespace from ai-search-provider

For AI Search, use ai-search-provider. For more information, refer to Models.

Basin SQL supports OFFSET

Basin SQLBasin

Basin SQL is a serverless, distributed SQL engine for querying Apache Iceberg tables in Basin Catalog. It now supports OFFSET, which lets you skip a specified number of rows when retrieving query results.

Use LIMIT to set the page size and OFFSET to skip earlier rows. With a page size of 100, use OFFSET 0 for the first page, OFFSET 100 for the second, and increase the offset by 100 for each later page. Add ORDER BY on a unique column to keep the row order consistent.

For example, this query returns the second page of 100 rows:

For syntax and examples, refer to the OFFSET clause in the Basin SQL reference.

Oct 21, 2026

Account-scoped HTTP request logs in Logpush

LogpushLogs

Cloudflare Logpush now supports HTTP request logs as an account-scoped dataset. Use one job to deliver logs for every zone in an account instead of maintaining a separate job for each zone.

Create the job at the account level in the Cloudflare dashboard or through the Logpush API. The ZoneName field identifies the source zone in each log entry.

Custom fields remain configured per zone. An account-scoped job honors the custom fields configuration for each zone but does not support account-wide custom fields configuration.

For setup details, refer to API configuration.
